edits.value_json: 小 means “small.” Early examples use it with this meaning, while interpretations of the marks’ referent differ: they have been taken as abstract signs of smallness, raindrops or scattered objects, or fine sand grains.

小 has no settled account of what its early marks represent: analyses describe abstract signs of smallness, raindrops or scattered objects, or fine sand grains. The sand-grain account treats 小 as an early graph of 沙, but neither the depicted referent nor a sound-based borrowing is established. Accounts also describe 小 and 少 as sharing an early graph before they were differentiated; one account says 少’s lower dot became a diagonal stroke. In small-seal script, the central dot became a vertical stroke between two side marks. Shuowen’s analysis of this later form as 八 plus 丨 is a historical interpretation, not evidence of the original construction.
